texts.orig: IALC 0105. Community-Based Leadership Seminar. (0 Credits)
texts.text: IALC 0105. Community-Based Leadership Seminar. (0 Credits)

texts.label: text
texts.orig: This bilingual seminar is open to the community and explores multiple contexts and practices of leadership in the community. Special emphasis will be on developing leadership skills among participants by reading texts, case studies, completing self-assessments, and discussing topics related to agency and the impact of personal leadership as an agent of change in the community.

texts.orig: IALC 0106. Citizenship and Civic Engagement Seminar. (0 Credits)
texts.text: IALC 0106. Citizenship and Civic Engagement Seminar. (0 Credits)

texts.label: text
texts.orig: This course is open to participants in the community who plan to apply or have applied for naturalization. Special emphasis will be given to the topics that participants will discuss during the civics portion of their naturalization interview, such as American history, government and law, and geography of the United States.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: IALC 1005. Service Learning Project. (0 Credits)
texts.text: IALC 1005. Service Learning Project. (0 Credits)

texts.label: text
texts.orig: For students at CEFR level A2 and above. This course encourages student engagement in the local community through volunteer opportunities arranged in partnership with the Center for Community Engaged Learning at Fordham. Special emphasis is on promoting greater awareness of issues in the United States concerning equity, class status, race, and nationality through service-learning experience, readings, films, and discussions.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: IALC 1006. Academic Writing Seminar. (0 Credits)
texts.text: IALC 1006. Academic Writing Seminar. (0 Credits)

texts.label: text
texts.orig: CEFR: A2-B2+ This seminar provides a review of academic writing conventions. The seminar will help students organize, clarify, and support their ideas. Special attention will be given to revision and editing, structure and organization, paraphrasing and summarizing academic texts, critique and argumentation strategies, as well as a review of references, citations, and steps to avoid plagiarism.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: CEFR: A1-A2. This course is designed to strengthen students' comprehensive grammar integrated with reading and writing skills. texts.text: IALC 1150. Intermediate Reading, Writing, and Grammar 2. (0 Credits)

texts.label: text
texts.orig: For students at CEFR level A2 to B1. This course is designed to enhance students' comprehensive grammar integrated with intensive and extensive reading and writing skills. Special emphasis will be placed on developing scanning skills to gather information from different parts of a text, and writing connected texts by linking a series of shorter discrete elements into a linear sequence.
